title: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)

sections.label: MND COS budget cut motion
sections.summary: The Chairman moves to reduce Head T of the Estimates by $100, after the MND GPC consulted widely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head T of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Mr Chairman, in preparing for the Committee of Supply (COS), because MND touches on the lives of many Singaporeans, our Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) has consulted widely with our people, with industry experts, with housing experts and we have come today to put forward some of our ideas.

sections.label: Lowering BTO eligibility age for singles
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to a policy move to lower the BTO flat eligibility age to 33 for singles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Now that this critical group has their needs well met, it is time for us to consider how we can improve accessibility and affordability for others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I look forward to a timely policy move to lower the BTO flat eligibility age to, hopefully, 33 for singles.

sections.label: Access to 5-room BTOs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MND can consider giving access to 5-room BTOs immediately if net worth is comparable to typical HDB-dwelling families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If their net worth is comparable to typical HDB-dwelling families, can MND consider giving them access to 5-room BTOs immediately?

sections.label: Housing grant for ECs
sections.summary: ECs currently receive a housing grant of up to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: ECs currently receive a housing grant of up to $30,000.

sections.label: Building higher than 50 storeys
sections.summary: One option is to build higher, beyond 40 and 50 storeys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One is to build higher, beyond 40 and 50 storeys.

sections.label: Releasing greenfield and brownfield sites
sections.summary: Keeping housing accessible and affordable must be matched by willingness to identify and release suitable greenfield and brownfield sites in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If we are determined to keep housing accessible and affordable, then that same determination must also be matched by our willingness to identify and release suitable greenfield and brownfield sites in a timely manner.

sections.label: Construction spending projections
sections.summary: Construction spending is projected to exceed $50 billion over the next few years, including Terminal 5, Marina Bay Sands expansion, MRT and HDB works, before tapering to around $40 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Over the next few years, construction spending is projected to exceed $50 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We are powering ahead with Terminal 5, I think we are expanding on the Marina Bay Sands, there is a lot of underground and Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) construction and more HDBs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And this $50 billion will be for two years before tapering to around $40 billion.

sections.label: HDB income ceilings
sections.summary: Some are unable to buy flats due to HDB income ceilings, currently $14,000 for a couple seeking a BTO flat and $16,000 for ECs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For some, they are unable to do so arising from the income ceiling imposed by HDB, currently set at $14,000 for a couple looking for a BTO flat, with $16,000 set as the ceiling for ECs.

sections.label: Subsidy clawback regime
sections.summary: The subsidy clawback regime started at around 6% and is now at 14% for some BTO developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One example is the subsidy clawback regime which started at around 6% and is now at 14% for some BTO developments.

sections.label: Appeals against income ceiling
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to share how many appeals were received from first-time applicants unable to buy a BTO flat due to the income eligibility ceiling each year from 2020 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, Sir, can the Minister also share how many appeals it has received from first-time applicants who sought to purchase a BTO flat but could not do so because of the income eligibility ceiling for each year from 2020 to 2025?

sections.label: HDB shop tenancy terms
sections.summary: On 10 January 2026, amid public concerns about rising commercial rents, HDB announced successful bidders for HDB shops must commit to tendered rates for two tenancy terms totalling six years instead of one three-year term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 10 January 2026, on the back of public concerns about rising commercial rents, HDB announced, amongst other things, that successful bidders for any HDB shops would have to commit to their tendered rates for over two tenancy terms totalling six years instead of one three-year term to encourage prudent bidding.

sections.label: HDB commercial rental transparency
sections.summary: The speaker calls for public sublet rental information, reporting and publishing of all HDB commercial rentals on a central portal, and an independent council to monitor market rental rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For a subset of the shops, namely coffee shops, HDB acknowledges that some lessees may impose high mark-up rentals on individual stallholders even as the rent paid by these operators to HDB have remained largely unchanged or stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I called on HDB to make public sublet rental information in October 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The HDB's announcement of 10 January 2026 indicates that the HDB has committed to collect data on stall rents charged by operators before it determines how the data can be made available publicly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would suggest that all HDB commercial rentals, including, if sublet, ought to be made reportable and published on an easily accessible central portal or platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the majority of HDB commercial properties are in private hands with the basic details of current rental rates available elsewhere, it would not be difficult for HDB to provide this information on the same centralised portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would give market players and new entrants, particularly small businesses an easy reference point and a clear-eyed perspective on their rental-related business decisions in the HDB commercial space, regardless of whether the landlord is HDB or a private owner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of recent incidents regarding dissatisfaction with rising rental prices, I propose that a council, like the Public Transport Council, an independent regulatory Statutory Board and in this case, under MND, be established to monitor rental rates in the market.

sections.label: Rental price increase range
sections.summary: Rental price increases of 3% to 15% are generally acceptable, while growth beyond this range should be reviewed before approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, it is generally acceptable for rental prices to increase between 3% and 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Any growth beyond this range should be reviewed closely and carefully before a decision being made to approve or disallow to proceed.

sections.label: Resale HDB and EC prices
sections.summary: Per square foot prices for resale HDB flats and ECs rose from 2016 to 2024, with the difference reaching 154%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2016, the average per square foot price for a resale HDB flat stood at approximately $424, and approximately $782 for an EC in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2021, the resale HDB flat per square foot price stands at $488 versus $1,176 for an EC, a 141% difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Coming to 2024, a resale HDB flat is approximately $603 per square foot and $1,531 for an EC, a 154 % difference.

sections.label: New EC versus resale HDB
sections.summary: In 2025, the average new EC price is $1.7 million versus $652,000 for a resale HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fast forward to 2025, the average price of a new EC is $1.7 million compared to $652,000 for a resale HDB flat, a difference of more than $1 million.

sections.label: EC affordability and loan shortfall
sections.summary: A household faces a shortfall of just over $700,000 for an EC and just over $400,000 for a private condominium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would mean a shortfall of just over $700,000 based on the price of an average EC today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the same household will be able to secure a loan of close to $1.28 million, leaving a smaller shortfall of just over $400,000 should they choose to purchase a private condominium instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Other than simply giving more grants, two other simple solutions are to raise the mortgage servicing ratio, which would enable households to take on higher mortgage to finance a property and to increase the monthly household income ceiling to allow more buyers into the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perversely, these may even result in an even higher increase in EC prices, given the wider pool of buyers now available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, given the increasing unaffordability of ECs in the markets today, I urge the MND to seriously re-think the current EC model and to consider upstream policies to bring the price of ECs into a range that will suit their original intentions.

sections.label: MOP for flat types
sections.summary: The MOP is five years for standard flats and 10 years for Plus and Prime flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the case of standard flats, the MOP is five years, while for the Plus and Prime flats, it is 10 years.

sections.label: Singapore total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate is 0.87, below the replacement level of 2.1.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore is facing a critically low total fertility rate of 0.87, way below the replacement level of 2.1.

sections.label: Young couples housing affordability
sections.summary: Median households crossing $12,000 leaves many young couples ineligible for BTO or PPHS support yet priced out of resale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With median households crossing $12,000, many young couples are trapped – ineligible for BTO or Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) support, yet priced out of the resale market.

sections.label: Lowering BTO eligibility age
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will weigh lowering the BTO eligibility age from 35 so couples can anchor futures earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the Government weigh the call to lower the BTO eligibility age from 35, allowing them to anchor their futures earlier?

sections.label: Rental households transitioning to ownership
sections.summary: In 2020, Parliament heard only 2% of public rental households transition to home ownership each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2020, Parliament heard that only 2% of public rental households transition to home ownership at each year.

sections.label: Targets for rental household ownership
sections.summary: It asks what targets the Minister set to increase rental households transitioning to home ownership each year up to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Minister: what targets has the Minister set to increase the number of rental households transitioning to home ownership for each year, up to 2030?

sections.label: Government co-owner equity scheme
sections.summary: The Government would hold perhaps 20% equity as co-owner, with buyers putting down only 2% in cash or CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government would step in as co-owner, holding perhaps 20% equity in the flat, and instead of the standard down payment, the buyer would only need to put down 2% in cash or CPF, a much lower barrier to entry.

sections.label: Senior HDB households share
sections.summary: A study from October 2023 to April 2024 found senior households aged 65 and above form one-third of all HDB households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A study conducted, between October 2023 and April 2024, found that senior households where the decision-maker is aged 65 and above now form one-third of all HDB households, up from one quarter in 2018.

sections.label: Seniors monetising flats for repairs
sections.summary: Monetising flats through renting rooms or the Lease Buyback Scheme is meant to supplement retirement income and medical expenses, not to fund basic repairs for seniors ageing-in-place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some may argue that if seniors wish to continue ageing-in-place, but do not have the cash to afford the renovations needed, they can monetise their flats through renting out rooms or through the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS), but these schemes are primarily meant to supplement retirement income and medical expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Seniors should not be put in a position where they need to consider monetising their homes just to afford basic repairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will help seniors ageing-in-place, especially those who are living alone, without any next of kin to support them financially or mentally – to do so with dignity, safety and basic comfort.

sections.label: Aged Well Neighbourhoods announcement
sections.summary: The Prime Minister announced the Aged Well Neighbourhoods at last year's National Day Rally to support seniors who prefer to age at home in areas with high senior populations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister announced the "Aged Well Neighbourhoods" at last year's National Day Rally to support seniors who prefers to age at home, where there are high senior populations.

sections.label: Renewal bids 86% higher
sections.summary: In one recent renewal, bids were up to 86% higher than the previous contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In one recent renewal, bids were up to 86% higher than the previous contract.

sections.label: Government grants for town councils
sections.summary: The Government provides about $240 million annually through grants such as the S&CC Operating Grant, Lift Maintenance Grant and Lift Replacement Fund Matching Grant, and in 2023 MND introduced time-limited special funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government has been providing substantial support, about $240 million annually, through grants, such as the S&CC Operating Grant, the Lift Maintenance Grant and the Lift Replacement Fund Matching Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In 2023, MND also introduced a time-limited special funding to help cushion cost increases and moderate S&CC adjustments.

sections.label: Questions on S&CC support
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MND will review the S&CC Operating Grant baseline, study additional support for estates with ageing blocks, and clarify long-term cost-sharing and transitional funding for the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: First, because given that the cost increases arising from the Progressive Wage Model and regulatory changes are structural rather than cyclical, will MND consider reviewing the baseline quantum of S&CC Operating Grant to reflect new cost realities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, can MND study whether additional support can be provided for estates with a higher proportion of ageing blocks, where maintenance intensity is clearly higher?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, regarding the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, can MND provide clarity on the long-term cost-sharing model and whether transitional funding will be available?

sections.label: Details on HIP II
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to share more details on the scope, scale and implementation timeline of HIP II, which was mentioned as more extensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: He mentioned that HIP II would be more extensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, could I ask the Minister to share more details on the scope, the scale and the implementation timeline of HIP II?

sections.label: VERS compensation for affected homeowners
sections.summary: The MP urges the Ministry to make the baseline VERS compensation package one where affected homeowners need no cash top-up for a replacement flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But this is hardly ideal for affected homeowners who are most probably senior, no longer working and decumulating wealth to fund retirement life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Ministry to consider making the baseline VERS deal, the baseline VERS compensation package, one in which an affected homeowner will not need to top up cash for a new replacement flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: This, in turn, effectively means that the Government may have to come in and subsidise the cash top-up for affected homeowners instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The Government will effectively have to pay a premium beyond market value to achieve fairness for current, affected homeowners.

sections.label: Lease Buyback Scheme market value
sections.summary: The Government already pays market value for leases under the Lease Buyback Scheme to homeowners who remain in their current properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The Government is already paying market value for leases under the Lease Buyback Scheme to homeowners who remain in situ, in their current properties.

sections.label: Air-conditioning in public rental flats
sections.summary: In response to a Parliamentary Question filed in October, only 7,000 of more than 50,000 public rental flats have air-conditioning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: In response to a Parliamentary Question I filed in October, I note only 7,000 of more than 50,000 public rental flats have air-conditioning.

sections.label: Proposed ACCESS scheme under ComLink+
sections.summary: Noting the existing EASE programme for seniors, the MP proposes a new ACCESS scheme under ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: We already have the EASE programme for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: I propose a new ACCESS scheme under ComLink+.

sections.label: Social and Heritage Impact Assessment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will implement a formal Social and Heritage Impact Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: Will the Ministry implement a formal Social and Heritage Impact Assessment?

sections.label: ABC Waterways network span
sections.summary: The ABC Waterways network spans 8,000 kilometres through Singapore's homes and communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: Furthermore, our ABC Waterways network spans 8,000 kilometres through our homes and communities.

sections.label: HDB LUP cost cap reversal
sections.summary: HDB wrote in September 2024 that a block's LUP cost exceeded the cost cap, but changed its mind about 12 months later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: On 6 September 2024, HDB replied in writing to my appeal for a Block 363 resident, stating explicitly that the cost per flat had, I quote, "exceeded the LUP cost cap substantially, hence, we are unable to implement LUP", unquote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Yet, barely 12 months later, HDB changed their minds.

sections.label: LUP blocks feasibility figures
sections.summary: The Minister's reply revealed 100 of 140 blocks without full same floor lift access remain unfeasible, and LUP will extend to 40 more blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Minister for National Development's reply to my Parliamentary Question of 3 February 2026 revealed that of the 140 blocks in Singapore with no full same floor lift access, 100 blocks remain unfeasible, because cost of LUP exceeds $200,000 per unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Minister also said that LUP will be extended to the other 40 more blocks progressively.

sections.label: Residents want to stay home
sections.summary: Despite the lift access housing grant rising to $80,000, many affected residents say they do not want to be uprooted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding increase of the value of the lift access housing grant to $80,000, many affected residents have told me that they do not want to be uprooted and they want to stay in their homes with dignity.

sections.label: Requests on LUP timeline and cap
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to define a timeline for the 40 blocks and to remove the hard cap for the remaining 100 blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Whether it is a historical architectural debt or an HDB debt, providing same floor lift access is only fair to all HDB homeowners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask the Minister: one, please define a clear timeline for LUP for the 40 blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Two, please consider removing the proposed hard cap for the remaining 100 blocks and set aside a dedicated final amount to fund for LUP.

sections.label: Urging final mile lift access
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to bridge the final mile so every HDB homeowner can age in place with same floor lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we must not let the remaining residents without same floor lift access, be defined by the technical limits of a bygone era.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to bridge this final mile and ensure that every HDB homeowner can edge in place with the dignity of same floor lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Chairman, we note that about 100 HDB blocks are unable to benefit from the LUP, mainly because the estimated cost exceeds $200,000 per flat.

sections.label: Extending grant to seniors 70
sections.summary: The speaker hopes HDB will extend the Lift Access Housing Grant to households with at least one occupier aged 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, many seniors aged 70 and above may not yet be severely immobile, but face progressive decline and rising fall risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We hope HDB can consider extending the Lift Access Housing Grant to households where at least one occupier is aged 70 and above, similar to the criteria to qualify for a personal mobility aid.

sections.label: MND pest bird feedback cases
sections.summary: MND receives about 22,000 cases of public feedback on pest birds every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Chairman, every year, MND receives about 22,000 cases of public feedback on pest birds.

sections.label: Pest bird management strategy proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MND strengthen funding and manpower and develop a national strategy with measurable outcomes on pest birds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Chairman, I propose that MND strengthen dedicated funding and manpower for pest bird management and develop a clear national strategy with measurable outcomes to reduce cases, attacks and environmental nuisance over the next few years.

sections.label: Diseases in pest bird droppings
sections.summary: Their droppings carry dangerous diseases such as cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis and psittacosis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Their droppings carry dangerous diseases, such as cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis and psittacosis.

sections.label: NParks pilot expansion timeline
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a timeline to extend the NParks pilot to remaining Town Councils and proposes shortening the 35-unit netting trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The NParks pilot began in July, 2024, with three Town Councils and only expanded to three more in June 2025 nearly a year later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With many estates still experiencing persistent pigeon problems, can the Minister provide a clear timeline for extending this programme to all remaining Town Councils?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Regarding the 35-unit netting trial, I propose that the Ministry consider reducing the trial duration to gather sufficient data more quickly.

sections.label: Animal welfare legislation plans 2026
sections.summary: The question asks what the Ministry's specific plans for 2026 are regarding animal welfare legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's specific plans for 2026 regarding animal welfare legislation?

sections.label: Crow shooting safeguards in estates
sections.summary: The question asks what safeguards minimise public exposure, especially young children, during crow shooting operations in estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With crow shooting as the latest control measure, I would like to ask: on the protocols, particularly on the use of shooting in residential areas; what safeguards are in place to minimise public exposure, especially to young children, during such operations in estates.

sections.label: S Pass salary domino effect
sections.summary: Periodic raising of S Pass qualifying salaries creates a domino effect that unnecessarily increases business costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The periodic raising of S Pass qualifying salaries creates a "domino effect", jacking up business costs unnecessarily.

sections.label: Redesigning construction careers locally
sections.summary: MND is asked how it will redesign construction careers to attract and anchor a sizable local talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will MND redesign construction careers to attract and anchor a sizable local talent pool?

sections.label: Green cover 40% of land
sections.summary: Despite extensive urbanisation, green cover spans 40% of land area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Despite extensive urbanisation, our green cover spans a remarkable 40% of land area.

sections.label: Nature integration in housing estates
sections.summary: MND is asked how it weighed trade-offs and integrated nature into design for new housing estates, with 2030 targets laid out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, could MND share how it has weighed trade-offs and integrated nature, including preservation of existing flora and fauna into design principles for newer and upcoming housing estates towards improving heat resilience and tackling rising sea level challenges?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under MND's push for city nature, several 2030 targets have been laid out, including animal and plant species recovery plans, as well as forest, marine and coastal habitat restoration.

sections.label: Reviewing housing aspirations typologies
sections.summary: MND is asked how it reviewed housing aspirations and whether it can explore typologies like dual key or modular layouts for caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How has MND reviewed the housing aspirations of Singaporeans, and can MND consider exploring some unique typologies in upcoming projects, for example, dual key or modular layout suitable for caregiving?

sections.label: Population growth and HDB flats
sections.summary: From 1980 to 2025 resident population grew from 2.4 million to 4.2 million and HDB flats more than tripled from 330,000 to over 1.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Between 1980 and 2025, the resident population has grown from 2.4 million to 4.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the same time, the average household size has decreased from about five in 1980 to three in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, in this period, HDB has had to more than triple the number of flats from 330,000 to more than 1.2 million, all these while also meeting expectations to improve quality and design.

sections.label: Citizen marriages with non-residents
sections.summary: In the past three years, one in four citizen marriages were with a non-resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the past three years, one in four citizen marriages were with a non-resident.

sections.label: Unchanged $14,000 cap
sections.summary: The $14,000 cap has not changed since 2019 even though nominal wages have risen by more than 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: The $14,000 cap has not changed since 2019 even though nominal wages have risen by more than 25%.

sections.label: First-timer BTO application rates
sections.summary: Median application rates for first-timer families applying for 3-room and bigger BTO flats fell from almost seven times in 2020 to between 1.1 and 1.9 times in 2025, and were 0.9 times last month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The median application rates for first-timer families applying for 3-room and bigger BTO flats fell from a high of almost seven times in 2020 to between 1.1 and 1.9 times in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the most recent BTO sales exercise last month, the median application rate for first-timer families was 0.9 times.

sections.label: Building more homes faster
sections.summary: The Ministry prioritises building more homes faster, with HDB launching around 19,600 BTO flats this year, over 4,000 being Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Hence, a priority for the Ministry, which I have been emphasising since taking on the MND portfolio, is to build more homes and to build them faster.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This year, HDB will launch around 19,600 BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Of these, more than 4,000 will be Shorter Waiting Time flats, with a waiting time of less than three years.

sections.label: Tallest public housing project
sections.summary: The development will include Singapore's tallest ever public housing project, rising above 60 storeys.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The development will include Singapore's tallest ever public housing project, rising above 60 storeys.

sections.label: 60-storey block flat yield
sections.summary: A 60-storey block can provide 50% more flats compared to a 40-storey block, the height of most of our tallest HDB blocks today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: A 60-storey block can provide 50% more flats compared to a 40-storey block, the height of most of our tallest HDB blocks today.

sections.label: Toa Payoh parcel units
sections.summary: The parcel will have around 1,600 units, including public rental, 2-room Flexi, 4-room flats and Toa Payoh's first Community Care Apartments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The parcel will feature around 1,600 units, including public rental flats, 2-room Flexi and 4-room flats, and also, the first Community Care Apartments in Toa Payoh.

sections.label: Additional homes Toa Payoh Mount Pleasant
sections.summary: Over the next decade, more than 10,000 additional homes will be launched across Toa Payoh West and Mount Pleasant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Over the next decade, we will launch more than 10,000 additional homes across Toa Payoh West and Mount Pleasant.

sections.label: Income ceiling review BTO flats
sections.summary: The current income ceiling covers around eight in 10 Singaporean households, and the income ceiling for BTO flats is being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our current income ceiling covers around eight in 10 Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is because higher income earners can have access to other housing options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And as Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Cai Yinzhou noted, we are reviewing the income ceiling for BTO flats.

sections.label: Programme start and scaling up
sections.summary: The plan is to start with a few sites in the first half of the next decade, then scale up from late-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our plan is to start with a few sites in the first half of the next decade, before scaling up the programme from late-2030s.

sections.label: Private housing supply ramp up
sections.summary: About 12,000 units of private housing, including ECs, are expected to be launched for sale by developers this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Beyond public housing, we have also been ramping up private housing supply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We expect about 12,000 units of private housing, including ECs, to be launched for sale by developers this year.

sections.label: Resale flat price growth
sections.summary: Resale flat price growth slowed from 12.7% in 2021 to 2.9% in 2025, with prices flat in fourth quarter 2025 and a slight 0.1% decline in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Growth in resale flat prices has slowed from 12.7% in 2021, to 2.9% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the fourth quarter 2025, resale prices remained flat compared to the previous quarter, and this is the first time it has happened since first quarter 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As at mid-February, HDB resale prices for 2026 have shown a slight decline of 0.1%.

sections.label: EC versus private condominium prices
sections.summary: New EC sale prices are about 20% to 30% lower than comparable private condominiums.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: EC new sale prices are about 20% to 30% lower than comparable private condominiums.

sections.label: Sustainable development as MND priority
sections.summary: MND's third priority is developing Singapore sustainably by balancing land use requirements and trade-offs within limited space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The third priority for MND is to ensure that we continue developing Singapore sustainably for generations to come, by balancing different land use requirements and navigating trade-offs within the limited space we have.

sections.label: Optimising land use and conservation
sections.summary: Singapore will study new technologies, optimise under-utilised spaces, and preserve green, blue and heritage spaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Outram and Toa Payoh, which I spoke about earlier, are some examples.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will continue to study how we can harness new technologies, such as by building taller flats in other parts of Singapore and through the use of systems like the Pneumatic Waste Conveyance System, which frees up land for other uses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will also look at other ways of optimising land use, such as making better use of under-utilised spaces like the area under flyovers and MRT viaducts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As we develop and grow, we will keep an eye on conservation – preserving key green and blue spaces, and valuable pieces of our heritage.

sections.label: Development plans and skilled professionals needed
sections.summary: Singapore will build at least 80,000 homes in over 10 housing areas and needs at least 1,000 new architects and engineers yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will construct Changi Airport Terminal 5, redevelop Paya Lebar Air Base into a new-generation town, unlock the potential of the Greater Southern Waterfront and create Long Island to build homes and enhance coastal protection along the East Coast.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will build at least 80,000 new homes across more than 10 new housing areas island-wide over the next 10 to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To accomplish our ambitious development plans, we will need many more architects, engineers, quantity surveyors, project managers, builders and other skilled professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We estimate that over the next decade, we will need at least 1,000 new architects and engineers per year to join the sector and contribute towards Singapore's development.

sections.label: INSPIRE internship programme launched
sections.summary: An enhanced internship programme called INSPIRE was launched to deepen on-the-job learning, improve mentorship and enable higher starting salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To deepen the on-the-job learning, improve mentorship, and enable higher starting salaries, we have launched an enhanced internship programme called "INSPIRE".

sections.label: Higher internship allowance and starting salary
sections.summary: Firms will offer an internship allowance of at least $1,500 and a starting salary above market rate for interns who join after graduation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Firms will also offer a higher internship allowance of at least $1,500, and a higher starting salary above market rate if the intern joins them after graduation.

sections.label: Reduced Fee Score expansion
sections.summary: BCA expanded the Reduced Fee Score to public sector projects up to $100 million since December 2025, with 10 of 11 tenders awarded to highest quality scores.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Following the successful pilot of the "Reduced Fee Score", BCA has expanded the Reduced Fee Score to cover public sector projects up to $100 million since December 2025, to discourage fee-diving and put greater emphasis on quality-based procurement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The early results are promising – out of 11 tenders using the Reduced Fee Score since 2024, 10 were awarded to bids with the highest quality scores.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Limitation of Liability clause is now a default provision in the Standard Consultancy Agreement between Government Procuring Entities and consultants.

sections.label: Firms and service buyers commitment
sections.summary: Over 50 firms and service buyers have committed to it since September 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over 50 firms and service buyers have committed to it since September 2025.

sections.label: Strata Management Act review areas
sections.summary: A comprehensive review of the Building (Strata Management) Act will focus on sinking funds, consent thresholds, self-governance and stakeholder responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We must address these to ensure that these developments continue to be liveable and meet residents' needs, especially for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are undertaking a comprehensive review to strengthen the Building (Strata Management) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will focus on four key areas: first, helping MCSTs work towards accumulating adequate sinking funds for essential maintenance, repairs or upgrades; second, reducing consent thresholds for essential works; third, strengthening self-governance frameworks to promote fair and efficient management of estates; and fourth, clarifying the responsibilities of strata-titled stakeholders.

sections.label: Public consultations dates
sections.summary: Public consultations will be conducted from 9 March to 8 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To build on this, we will conduct public consultations from 9 March to 8 April 2026.

sections.label: Accessibility Fund senior features
sections.summary: The review will consider expanding Accessibility Fund funding to cover senior-related features such as fitness stations and dementia-friendly signages.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the review, we will consider expanding Accessibility Fund funding to cover senior-related features such as senior-friendly fitness stations and dementia-friendly signages.

sections.label: Flats set aside first-timers
sections.summary: At least 90% of 4-room and bigger flats are set aside for first-timer families, and about two-thirds who applied in 2023 and 2024 booked a flat.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The majority of these flats – at least 90% of 4-room and bigger flats – are set aside for first-timer families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: About two-thirds of first-timer families who applied in 2023 and 2024 were able to book a flat.

sections.label: TCPS quota and eligibility changes
sections.summary: TCPS quota doubles to 10% of BTO and SBF supply, and families qualify from expecting a third child, from June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, we will double the current TCPS quota from 5% of the BTO and SBF flat supply to 10% of the BTO and SBF flat supply.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Second, we will expand the eligibility criteria so that families can qualify for TCPS from the time when the mother is expecting her third child.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These changes will take effect from the June 2026 sales exercise.

sections.label: Bus service in new BTO estates
sections.summary: HDB and LTA will plan for at least one bus service to operate with the first key collection in new large-scale BTO estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To support transport connectivity, HDB and LTA will plan for at least one bus service to be operational in tandem with the first batch of key collection in new large-scale BTO estates.

sections.label: Rent-free period for HDB shops
sections.summary: Rent-free period for HDB shops rises from two to six months and for coffee shops from three to six months, for tenders from March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Next, HDB will increase the rent-free period for HDB shops in new BTO projects from two months to a maximum of six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Similarly, for coffee shops, their rent-free period will increase from the current three months to a maximum of six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This will apply to shop tenders from March 2026, and shops will need to start operations early to enjoy the maximum six-month rent-free period.

sections.label: Childcare centres in new BTO estates
sections.summary: Childcare centres in new large-scale BTO estates will commence operations within six months after the first residents collect their keys.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Taken together, childcare centres in new large-scale BTO estates will be up and running earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will plan for them to commence operations within six months after the first batch of residents collect their keys.

sections.label: Play framework for playgrounds
sections.summary: A published framework covering physical, social and creative play will be applied to new BTO playgrounds from 2026 and existing ones refreshed with Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The published framework emphasises three key aspects of play – physical, social and creative – to address the developmental needs of younger children aged two to five, and older children aged five to 12.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will apply the framework as we build new playgrounds in BTO projects from 2026, and we will work with Town Councils to refresh existing ones in other developed estates.

sections.label: Tendered rent for shop bidders
sections.summary: Successful bidders of all new shop tenders from January 2026 must maintain their tendered rent for two tenancy terms instead of one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To encourage prudent bids, successful bidders of all new shop tenders from January 2026 are required to maintain their tendered rent for two tenancy terms instead of one tenancy term of three years.

sections.label: HDB coffee shop rent data
sections.summary: HDB will collect data on stall rents charged by rental coffee shop operators, while IRAS holds records on privately-owned HDB shop tenancies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: HDB has announced in January 2026 that we will start collecting data on stall rents charged by rental coffee shop operators and we will look at how this data can be presented in an accessible way to the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For HDB sold shops which are in private hands, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) maintains records on lease and tenancy transactions of privately-owned HDB shops that are submitted to IRAS for the payment of stamp duty.

sections.label: Price-quality tenders for coffee shops
sections.summary: Since 2018, HDB has evaluated tender submissions for new coffee shops and new supermarkets using the price-quality method.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since 2018, HDB has evaluated tender submissions for new coffee shops and new supermarkets based on the “price-quality” method.

sections.label: Rent terms and stall rent data
sections.summary: Successful bidders must hold tendered rent for two tenancy terms, and HDB collects stall rent data from its coffee shop operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, to encourage rational bidding, successful bidders are required to maintain their tendered rent for two tenancy terms instead of one tenancy term of three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Second, to protect stall holders’ interests, HDB has begun collecting data on stall rents charged by coffee shop operators under its management in order to provide stall holders with more comprehensive and transparent rental information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, we will update our housing policies to support the diverse needs of different groups, including young couples, larger families and seniors.

sections.label: Integrated blocks and rental flats
sections.summary: Eight integrated blocks are completed and 36 are under construction, part of about 6,300 public rental flats to be completed in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: HDB has completed eight such integrated blocks and another 36 are under construction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Integrated blocks will form part of the approximately 6,300 public rental flats that will be completed over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: This will increase our total supply of rental flats while also helping to refresh some of our existing rental stock.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: It will also further bring down waiting times for rental flats, which has already improved from a high of 11 months during COVID-19 to an average of three months today.

sections.label: Fresh Start Housing Grant increase
sections.summary: Last year, the Fresh Start Housing Grant for eligible second-timer ComLink+ rental families was increased from $50,000 to $75,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Last year, we increased the Fresh Start Housing Grant for eligible second-timer ComLink+ rental families from $50,000 to $75,000.

sections.label: Rental households booking flats
sections.summary: Over 2,000 HDB rental households booked flats in 2025, and the Fresh Start Housing Scheme was extended to first-timer ComLink+ rental families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Throughout 2025, more than 2,000 HDB rental households have already booked HDB flats and are waiting for their completion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Last year, the Fresh Start Housing Grant for eligible Second-Timer ComLink+ rental families was increased from $50,000 to $75,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme was also extended to First-Timer ComLink+ rental families, enabling them to buy a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat on a shorter lease.

sections.label: LBS proceeds and bonus
sections.summary: From 2021 to 2025, a 4-room flat's average LBS proceeds plus LBS bonus was over $200,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: From 2021 to 2025, for a 4-room flat, the average LBS proceeds, including the portion used to top up the CPF Retirement Account, plus the LBS bonus received was over $200,000.

sections.label: Home Fire Alarm Devices
sections.summary: Home Fire Alarm Devices are installed in over 80% of public rental flats, with the rest progressively equipped at no cost to tenants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Mr Cai Yinzhou also mentioned technologies, such as fire and fall detection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We have installed Home Fire Alarm Devices in over 80% of our public rental flats, with the remainder being progressively equipped at no cost to tenants.

sections.label: Lift Upgrading Programme coverage
sections.summary: Since 2001, LUP gave direct lift access to 99% of HDB blocks; in 2025 it was announced for six blocks with about 40 more planned.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Since 2001, the LUP has brought direct lift access to 99% of our HDB blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: In 2025, LUP was announced for six blocks and there are plans for LUP to be extended to about 40 more blocks progressively.

sections.label: Grants to move for lifts
sections.summary: Eligible families and singles can receive up to $80,000 and $40,000 respectively to move to a flat with direct lift services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Eligible families and singles can receive up to $80,000 and $40,000 respectively, to move to a flat with direct lift services.

sections.label: Veterinary Council and Bill
sections.summary: A Veterinary Council will be established as a professional regulatory body, with the Veterinary Practice Bill introduced this week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: First, we will establish a Veterinary Council as a professional regulatory body to uplift standards for veterinary professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: It will also investigate cases of misconduct, where needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I will introduce the Veterinary Practice Bill to establish the proposed Council this week and I thank our veterinary sector and other stakeholders who have worked with us since 2021 to shape this Bill together.

sections.label: Pigeon Management Plan expansion
sections.summary: In June 2025, the Pigeon Management Plan was expanded to Jalan Besar, Marsiling-Yew Tee and Nee Soon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In June 2025, we expanded our Pigeon Management Plan to Jalan Besar, Marsiling-Yew Tee and Nee Soon.

sections.label: Wetlands by the Bay
sections.summary: Gardens by the Bay will welcome an all-new Wetlands by the Bay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Today, I am pleased to announce that Gardens by the Bay will welcome an all-new Wetlands by the Bay.

sections.label: Second marine park and research centre
sections.summary: A second marine park will be designated at Lazarus South and Kusu Reef, with $60 million for a marine science research centre hosted by NUS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Marine Park is a popular nesting site, with the turtle hatchery there, keeping baby turtles safe from human traffic, from predators and high tides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This year, we will formally designate a second marine park at Lazarus South and Kusu Reef to provide more opportunities for recreation, conservation, research and education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will therefore invest $60 million in a new marine science research centre of excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This Centre will be hosted by the National University of Singapore and supported by Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 funds.

sections.label: Consultation and environmental impact assessments
sections.summary: Projects in or near sensitive areas or with potential transboundary impact must undergo in-depth consultation, and an EIA is required if there is potential significant environmental impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Projects in, or near sensitive areas or that have potential transboundary impact, must undergo in-depth consultation with technical agencies, and we require an EIA if there is potential significant environmental impact from the development.

sections.label: Mount Pleasant estate heritage conservation
sections.summary: Six significant buildings are conserved with new uses, part of the former parade square retained, and these woven into a new Mount Pleasant estate of 6,000 homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: That is in Mr Cai's constituency, upcoming and opposite mine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have conserved six of the most significant buildings and given them new uses, including as a Neighbourhood Police Post and an SPF Heritage Gallery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will also retain part of the former parade square as a public space for community use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will weave these elements into a new Mount Pleasant estate that will bring 6,000 homes together with heritage and nature.

sections.label: Conserving grandstands and saddle club clubhouse
sections.summary: The two grandstands and the former Bukit Timah saddle club clubhouse will be conserved and integrated into future developments, with over 7,200 buildings and structures conserved today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Even as we transform the site into a housing estate, we will conserve the two grandstands that once housed thousands of spectators, as well as the former Bukit Timah saddle club clubhouse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will sensitively adapt and integrate these landmarks into future developments to keep the area's history alive  Today, we have conserved over 7,200 buildings and structures.

sections.label: AI routing of cases
sections.summary: Backend systems with AI and smart routing capabilities will direct about 90% of cases to the right agency or Town Council.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Our backend systems will do the rest, with AI and smart routing capabilities directing about 90% of cases to the right agency or Town Council.

sections.label: Reviewing more build sites
sections.summary: The speaker says the review is ongoing, no timeline can be given yet, and more land is being sought to build more and faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is something which we are actively looking at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I am unable at this point in time to give him a concrete timeline, but certainly we will be ready to share this when the review is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The answer is yes, we are going to look for more places where we can do this, and that is why I shared earlier that we need to look for more land that we can prepare the site to build more, build faster.

sections.label: HDB supply and household fragmentation
sections.summary: Household numbers rose despite smaller household size, and HDB will keep up robust supply beyond the committed 55,000 flats in three years if demand stays strong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Even though the number of people in the household, the average household size, may have come down, the number of households have actually increased because of this household fragmentation that we are seeing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I have said earlier that if demand remains strong, HDB will continue with this robust supply and we will go beyond what we earlier committed, which is to build 55,000 in three years.

sections.label: Lift access for households
sections.summary: The speaker assures Members that the intent is to try to provide lift access to as many households as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The assurance I want to give Members, as my colleague Senior Parliamentary Secretary Harun mentioned earlier, is that we will do our best, because it is our intent to try and provide lift access to as many households as possible.

sections.label: Rental to home ownership transition
sections.summary: No annual targets are set for rental households moving to home ownership, and 2,000 rental families were helped to transit last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: In terms of targets, we do not set any annual targets with regards to the transition from rental households to home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: As I have shared in my speech earlier, in the last year alone, we have helped 2,000 rental families transit in terms of their plans to home ownership and they are waiting for their flats.

sections.label: Lift Access Housing Grant eligibility
sections.summary: Eligibility is based on needs rather than age, requires a medical condition causing difficulty with stairs, and there are no plans to expand criteria by age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: The eligibility is assessed based on needs rather than the age of residents and one of the requirements is that there must be a medical condition for which this particular family member or this particular owner has difficulty in terms of mobility and navigating the stairs, which present as a limiting factor at this point of time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: We currently do not have any plans to expand the Lift Access Housing Grant criteria based on age.

sections.label: 60-storey towns not pinpointed
sections.summary: The speaker says it is too early to pinpoint which towns besides Pearl's Hill can have 60 storeys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the first question about 60 storeys, I think it is a bit too early for us to pinpoint which towns we are going to be able to do this, besides the one at Pearl's Hill that I just announced.

sections.label: 2-room Flexi flat supply review
sections.summary: Supply of 2-room Flexi flats will increase by about 50% over three years, and a review is considering allowing some singles to buy bigger flats with family.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Minister Chee, would you like to go first?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And that is why I mentioned earlier in my speech that we are going to increase the supply of 2-room Flexi flats by about 50% over the next three years to be able to meet this strong demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Looking ahead, I think we are also reviewing whether for some groups of singles who may not want to buy a 2-room Flexi on their own but they may want to buy with a family member, but they need a bigger flat, whether that is something that we can also allow, if we are able to have adequate supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I cannot give a timing on when we can review this as well because it really depends on when we feel confident about the supply being adequate.

sections.label: New group competing for BTO flats
sections.summary: Allowing a currently ineligible group would let them apply for the same BTO flat supply as the eight in 10 buyers below the income ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For example, if you allow this group – currently they are not eligible – if you allow them to come in, they will then apply for the same stock, the same supply of BTO flats that the other buyers, the eight out 10 who are currently below the income ceiling, this group will come in and compete with them for this supply of BTO flats.

sections.label: Second Marine Park intent
sections.summary: The second Marine Park is intended to safeguard ecologically significant habitats and enhance biodiversity on Sisters' Island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For the second Marine Park, the intent is to safeguard the ecologically significant habitats around the area, and also to enhance the existing biodiversity with the existing ones on Sisters' Island.

sections.label: Marine Science Centre research coordination
sections.summary: The new Marine Science Centre is a nationally coordinated research programme that will work with the Oceanarium and others on marine science and biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With regards to the Marine Science Centre, it is a nationally coordinated research programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, the new Marine Science Centre will in fact work with the Oceanarium and others to coordinate research about marine science capabilities and biodiversity.

sections.label: Public rental income ceiling
sections.summary: There has been no income ceiling for public rental housing since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: With regard to the income ceiling for public rental housing, just to reassure the Member, as well as Members here, that there is no income ceiling for public rental since 2023.

sections.label: HDB supply levels plan
sections.summary: A question asks whether HDB supply is still planned to come down to about 15,700 from the 19,600 levels today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: On the HDB front, is it still the plan to have the supply come down to about 15,700 or so, versus the 19,600 levels today.

sections.label: EC grant and developer prices
sections.summary: Increasing grants risks EC developers capturing public funds instead of home buyers, since EC prices are set by developers' bids and sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If it is something that we can do by just increasing the grant, that is quite direct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But in this case, if that is the move that we make, and because we do not control the EC prices – these are based on what developers bid and what they sell – there is a risk that much of the support given, which is going to come from taxpayers, public funds, will be creamed off by the EC developers, instead of going to the home buyers, which was the intent.

sections.label: Supply pipeline beyond 55,000
sections.summary: The supply pipeline will not be limited to the 55,000 previously mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: On supply pipeline, I have actually addressed this earlier in my response to some of the earlier clarifications that we are not going to keep ourselves limited to the 55,000, which is what I said earlier as well.

sections.label: Releasing private residential supply
sections.summary: If demand stays strong, capacity can be released via new Government Land Sale sites or converting reserve sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Private residential, same thing, I have also said this previously that if the demand remains strong, we do have some capacity that we can release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There are two ways to do this: we can either activate a new site and release it through the Government Land Sale programme; or we could convert some of the sites from reserve to the Government Land Sale programme, or put some new sites into reserve that the developers could trigger if the demand is strong.

sections.label: Lift waiting and maintenance costs
sections.summary: Residents set aside at least 15 minutes for lifts, and maintaining these lifts costs more than typical HDB flats despite higher S&CC charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: And two, a lot of them tell me that they set aside at least 15 minutes to catch the lift, for the fear of having to wait for a long time, especially when one of the lifts is broken down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: But the reality is that while they pay higher S&CC charges, the cost of maintaining this lift is actually more than for other typical HDB flats.

sections.label: Lift access for 40 blocks
sections.summary: No exact number is available now, but lift access for the 40 blocks is to be achieved within the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Unfortunately, I do not have the exact number now, but I can assure you that within the next few years, we endeavour to actually achieve the lift access specific to these 40 blocks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: But I will give you a sharper answer as soon as I have it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have really sparred on this many times and I had already mentioned that Lorong Halus did not require an EIA because the agencies assessed that it is not a sensitive nature area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have a broader approach which I have articulated both in the Adjournment Motion as well as earlier on in my expansive reply.

sections.label: Limited land and management
sections.summary: Singapore has little land, and all of it needs to be managed, which must be stated upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, taking a step back, that is important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We do not have a lot of land, and we need to manage all of these, and we need to say this upfront.

sections.label: 15-month wait-out period monitoring
sections.summary: The resale market will be monitored further, with a slight 0.1% dip up to mid-February this quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Ms Lee had a question about the 15-month wait-out period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, as I have explained earlier, we will monitor the situation in the resale market a little bit more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Up to the middle of February this quarter, there was a slight dip, very slight, minus 0.1%.

sections.label: Netting solution trial specifications
sections.summary: The trial for the 35 units of the netting solution is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: And the other one is, would the Ministry be willing to share the specifications of the netting solution being trialled with Town Councils, so that Town Councils that wish to proceed may carry out their own installations in affected estates without having to wait out for the conclusion of the trial?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I would just say that the trial for the 35 units is ongoing.

sections.label: Progress for 40 blocks
sections.summary: The progress for the 40 blocks identified will be implemented within the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Just to give a sharper response to Mr Tan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: We will be looking to implement the progress for the 40 blocks identified within the next three years.
